summary: Backend-only multi-tenant isolation testing (org A = admin@mikilab.de/org_default vs org B = freshly registered Capo via activation_code=198505 → new org_id). Executed 7 pytest tests against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. ALL 7 PASS. Verified: (1) sessions distinct, (2) inventory GET/PUT do not leak across orgs, (3) favorites toggle/get + favorites/counts are org-scoped (B's counts hide A's recipe_ids and vice versa), (4) day-close list/last/{id}/pdf strictly filtered by org — cross-org PDF fetch returns 404, (5) recipes personal: create/list (include_mine=true) hidden across orgs; PUT/DELETE/translate/promote of A's recipe by B returns 403/404, (6) weekly-plan GET returns per-user+per-org doc with retro-compat fallback, no leakage of A marker into B and vice versa, (7) regression: org_default still receives MikiLab public recipes (GET /api/recipes?collection_name=mikilab returns >0 items).
critical_code_review_comments: recipes.py save_weekly_plan (L588-590): the update_one filter uses only {"_key": user_id} without organization_id. This is fine because _key is user-scoped (one weekly plan per user) and the $set writes organization_id, but for defence-in-depth consider including organization_id in the filter to avoid rewriting a plan that (via legacy data) belongs to another org sharing the same _key. Currently benign since _key == user_id and users belong to a single org.

recipes.py get_weekly_plan retrocompat branch (L580) matches ANY legacy doc without organization_id for the given user_id. Since users are org-bound, this is safe, but the retrocompat doc will be returned regardless of the caller's current org — acceptable for migration.

server.py get_recipes (L2820): mikilab collection is filtered by organization_id — good — but seed_mikilab_if_empty() may not seed per-org. Verified that org_default still sees seeded MikiLab recipes; new orgs (like org B) will receive an empty MikiLab list until seeded — expected per spec (isolation) but worth confirming with product owner.
operations.py inventory_save (L635) deletes-then-inserts using {owner_id, organization_id} filter — correct. _notify_low_stock is passed org — correct.
